title: Private Observability Minimum Pack — Operator Install Guide (VPC + On‑Prem)
author: Elliot Price
body:
## Summary
The **Private observability minimum pack** is the baseline, supported set of:
- **Dashboards** (gateway/API, runtime performance, GPU saturation, control plane health, install/upgrade health)
- **Alert rules** (SLO burn, availability/latency/error, resource exhaustion, queueing/saturation, pipeline health, missing signals)
- **Log pipeline defaults** (structured logs + recommended collector configuration and filters)

This guide covers how to install the pack in **Redwood Private** for both **VPC** and **on‑prem (including air‑gapped)** deployments.

## Goals / non-goals
**Goals**
- “Day‑1 usable” metrics/log dashboards and alerts without bespoke work.
- Consistent signals across VPC and on‑prem.
- Secure-by-default setup (no secrets in dashboards; least-privilege access; TLS guidance).

**Non-goals**
- Building a new observability backend.
- Customer-specific dashboards/alert tuning beyond the baseline.

---

## Supported components (minimum pack)
The minimum pack is **tested and supported** with the following components and integration patterns.

### Metrics + alert evaluation
- **Prometheus** (self-managed)
  - Rule format: Prometheus recording rules + alerting rules (PrometheusRule-style bundles may be installed via Helm in Kubernetes environments).
  - Alert delivery: Prometheus Alertmanager is recommended.

### Dashboards
- **Grafana** (customer-managed or pack-provisioned depending on install mode)
  - Provisioning supported via Grafana provisioning APIs/files.
  - Authentication: see “Security defaults” below.

### Logs
- **Collector/forwarder**: Fluent Bit **or** Vector
  - Supported outputs: customer SIEM (Syslog/HTTP), customer object storage/log archive, or customer-managed log backend.
  - The pack provides: structured log field expectations, recommended filters/sampling knobs, and pipeline health alerts.

> Note: The pack works in both VPC and on‑prem. In **air‑gapped** environments, all container images and chart assets must be mirrored internally (see “Air‑gapped/on‑prem notes”).

---

## Prerequisites
### Access / permissions
- Cluster access with permissions to:
  - Install/upgrade Helm releases in the Redwood Private namespace(s)
  - Create/modify ConfigMaps, Secrets, and (if applicable) PrometheusRule resources
  - Read logs from gateway/runtime/control plane pods
- Access to Grafana admin (or a service account token) if provisioning dashboards into an existing Grafana.

### Network
- Prometheus must be able to scrape metrics endpoints for:
  - **Gateway/API**
  - **Runtime**
  - **Control plane services** (Private)
  - **Installer/upgrade controller** (if deployed)
- Grafana must be able to reach Prometheus (or other configured metrics datasource) over the allowed network paths.

### Time + storage
- Ensure the metrics backend has sufficient capacity for baseline retention.
  - Default guidance for the min pack: **7–14 days** metrics retention (customer may choose higher).
- Ensure log forwarding path has adequate bandwidth; the pack is designed to support sampling/filters for high-volume workloads.

### Redwood versions / compatibility
- Redwood Private installer version must be compatible with the observability pack version you are installing.
- If you are upgrading an existing Private deployment, read the **Upgrade/Rollback Procedure** page before proceeding.

---

## What gets installed
Depending on your deployment mode, the install will apply some or all of the following:
- Grafana dashboard folders + dashboards + datasource templates
- Prometheus recording/alert rules (grouped; toggles available)
- Collector configuration (Fluent Bit or Vector) for structured log forwarding
- Validation checks (post-install report + missing signals checks)

### Key dashboard set (baseline)
- **Gateway / API overview**: RPS, p50/p95/p99 latency, 4xx/5xx rates, streaming disconnects
- **Runtime performance**: prefill vs decode, queue depth, batch sizes, cache hit rate
- **GPU saturation**: utilization, memory, throttling, correlation to latency/error
- **Control plane health**: auth integration health, policy/config services
- **Private install health**: installer/upgrade controller health, component readiness

### Key alert set (baseline)
- SLO burn-rate alerts (multi-window)
- Availability/latency/error alerts (high urgency, low noise)
- Resource exhaustion alerts (GPU/CPU/memory/disk)
- Queue buildup / saturation alerts
- Pipeline health alerts (log backlog/drops, export failures)
- “Missing signals” alerts (scrape failures, rules not loaded, dashboards unable to query)

---

## Security defaults (operator checklist)
Before enabling alert routing/paging, validate the following:
- **Grafana auth**: integrate with your IdP (SAML/OIDC) or enforce strong local auth.
- **Grafana permissions**:
  - Create a read-only “Operators” role for most users.
  - Restrict dashboard editing and datasource changes to a small admin group.
- **Audit expectations**:
  - Ensure Grafana access and admin actions are auditable per your org policy.
  - Ensure Prometheus/Alertmanager config changes are controlled and tracked.
- **No secret material in dashboards**:
  - The pack dashboards must not include tokens, client secrets, or raw headers.
- **TLS**:
  - Use TLS for Grafana and any log export endpoints that leave the cluster.

For regulated deployments, also review: *Private observability pack audit log considerations*.

---

## Installation paths
Use exactly one of the two installation paths below:
1) **Redwood Private Installer (recommended)** — standard supported path
2) **Helm-based installation (advanced)** — used when customer manages observability components and requires manual provisioning

---

## Path 1: Install via Redwood Private Installer (recommended)
### 1. Configure installer values
Set (or confirm) the observability pack options in your installer configuration.

Minimum required inputs:
- **observabilityPack.enabled**: true
- **observabilityPack.version**: pin a specific version (recommended for reproducibility)
- **metrics.backend**: Prometheus endpoint / service discovery configuration
- **grafana.mode**: pack-provisioned or customer-managed
- **logs.collector**: fluent-bit or vector
- **logs.export.target**: your SIEM/object storage/log backend target (as applicable)

If you do not have a log backend in day‑1, you may install dashboards and alert rules first and enable log forwarding later.

### 2. Run installation
From an operator workstation with access to the Private environment:
1) Run the installer apply step for the target environment.
2) Confirm the installer reports a pinned observability pack version.
3) Confirm Grafana provisioning step completes (or, if using customer-managed Grafana, confirm the provisioning artifacts were generated).

> Tip: When installing into an existing cluster, schedule the change during a low-traffic window; rule reloads and collector restarts are usually quick but can temporarily delay alert evaluation.

### 3. Enable alert delivery (Alertmanager)
- Ensure Alertmanager receivers are configured (email, PagerDuty, Opsgenie, etc.).
- Start with **ticketing / non-paging** routes for 24–72 hours in staging-like traffic if possible.
- Move only the high-urgency “page” alerts to paging routes after you confirm expected fire rates.

### 4. Post-install validation (installer command)
Run the installer’s post-install validation command (added for the minimum pack) to verify:
- Prometheus can scrape required endpoints
- Alert rules parse and load successfully
- Grafana API is reachable (if provisioning)
- Dashboards load and can query datasource
- Required metric series exist (minimum signals)

Capture the validation output and attach it to your go-live record.

---

## Path 2: Helm-based installation (advanced)
Use this path when:
- The customer runs Prometheus/Grafana outside the Redwood Private cluster, or
- The customer requires strict separation of duties where Redwood installer cannot provision Grafana

### 1. Install pack chart artifacts
1) Obtain the versioned observability pack bundle.
2) Apply the Kubernetes resources (ConfigMaps/Secrets/PrometheusRule objects) as documented for your environment.
3) If using Grafana provisioning files, mount/provision dashboards into the target Grafana instance.

### 2. Configure datasources and variables
- Verify the Grafana datasource points to the correct Prometheus.
- Confirm dashboards use the standard templated variables (cluster, namespace, tenant, model, route where applicable).

### 3. Configure log collector
- Deploy Fluent Bit or Vector with the recommended pipeline.
- Ensure redaction is enabled per your policy.
- Confirm export target connectivity and retry behavior.

### 4. Validation
Perform the same checks as “Post-install validation” below.

---

## Air‑gapped / on‑prem notes
### Offline artifacts
For air‑gapped installs, you must have:
- All required container images mirrored to an internal registry
- Helm charts and the observability pack bundle available in an offline artifact store
- A pinned version manifest (installer + charts + pack version)

### Connectivity assumptions
- No external egress is required for the pack itself.
- Exporting logs to an external SIEM is customer-dependent; if egress is restricted, route logs to an internal collector/relay or internal archive.

### Operational recommendation
- Use “minimal footprint” mode first (single Prometheus + single Grafana) unless the customer explicitly requires HA.
- Validate storage IOPS for Prometheus before increasing retention.

---

## Post-install validation checklist (operator)
This checklist is intentionally concrete; treat it as the **definition of a usable install**.

### A) Prometheus target health
- [ ] All required scrape targets are **UP**:
  - Gateway/API metrics target
  - Runtime metrics target(s)
  - Control plane metrics targets
  - Installer/upgrade metrics target (if applicable)
- [ ] Scrape errors are < 1% and stable.

### B) Rule loading health
- [ ] All alerting/recording rules load without parse errors.
- [ ] No “rule evaluation failures” at steady state.
- [ ] Rule group toggles reflect your environment (staging vs prod).

### C) Grafana provisioning and dashboards
- [ ] Grafana is reachable and authenticated via approved mechanism.
- [ ] Dashboards exist in the expected folders:
  - Private / Gateway
  - Private / Runtime
  - Private / GPU
  - Private / Control plane
  - Private / Install health
- [ ] Each dashboard loads without datasource errors.
- [ ] Key panels show non-empty data under normal traffic.

### D) Logs pipeline
- [ ] Collector daemonset/agents are running and stable.
- [ ] Export path is healthy (no sustained retries/backlog/drops).
- [ ] Sample structured fields are present in exported logs (spot check):
  - request_id
  - tenant (if enabled)
  - model
  - route
  - error_code (when errors occur)
- [ ] Redaction is working (no secrets / auth headers / raw prompts if prohibited by policy).

### E) Alert delivery
- [ ] Test alert can be sent end-to-end to the configured receiver.
- [ ] Paging routes are only enabled for high-urgency alerts.

> If any of these fail, see the Day‑2 Ops Runbook and the Supported Signal Validation Checklist page for queries and pass/fail criteria.

---

## Common pitfalls (and how to avoid them)
### 1) Grafana provisioning fails due to RBAC
**Symptoms**: Dashboards not created; Grafana API returns 403/401.
**Fix**:
- Confirm the provisioning service account/token has dashboard write permissions.
- If using Kubernetes-mounted provisioning, confirm volume mounts and folder permissions.

### 2) Alert rules not loading after an upgrade
**Symptoms**: No alerts firing; Prometheus shows rule parse errors; promtool fails.
**Fix**:
- Validate you pinned a compatible pack version.
- Run rule linting/validation (promtool) on the installed bundle.
- Roll back to the last known-good version if needed.

### 3) “Empty dashboards” due to label mismatch or high cardinality guardrails
**Symptoms**: Panels show no data or “No series found.”
**Fix**:
- Confirm required metric labels exist (tenant/model/route where expected).
- Confirm metrics relabeling is not dropping required labels.
- Do not add high-cardinality labels (request_id) to metrics.

### 4) Log export drops events under load
**Symptoms**: SIEM shows gaps; collector reports drops/backpressure.
**Fix**:
- Enable or increase sampling for high-volume log categories.
- Increase buffer limits and ensure disk space for buffering where configured.
- Confirm network throughput and retry/backoff settings.

### 5) Noisy alerts on day‑1
**Symptoms**: Frequent firing with low operator value.
**Fix**:
- Keep paging disabled initially; route to ticketing.
- Use the alert noise tuning workflow in the Day‑2 Ops Runbook.
- Prefer SLO burn alerts for paging; keep symptom alerts as non-paging or with longer for: windows.

---

## Escalation / supportability
When escalating to Redwood Support/Private Deployments, include:
- Observability pack version
- Private installer version
- Validation command output
- Screenshots (or exports) of:
  - Prometheus targets page
  - Prometheus rule load status
  - Grafana folder list
  - Collector logs showing export health
